about.heroTitle: We built the workshop first, then the studio
about.heroLead: Woodex Interior is a design-and-build practice in Lahore. Sixty-eight people: designers, project managers, forty-one craftsmen and site supervisors — all on our own payroll, all accountable to one programme.
about.splitText: Woodex began because our founders kept watching good drawings get ruined on site. Designers handed over a set, a contractor interpreted it, and nobody owned the gap between the two. So we bought the machines first.
about.splitText2: Eleven years later the same principle runs everything: the people who draw your space are the people who build it, and one project manager is accountable from the measured survey to the last snag.

about.splitQuote: Detail is not decoration. Detail is the reason a door closes quietly.

about.valuesTitle: Six principles that decide how we work
about.valuesText: They are not slogans. Each one changes something concrete about how a project is quoted, drawn, made or supervised.

values.title: Measure twice
values.text: Every project starts with a measured survey and an existing-conditions report. We would rather spend a day measuring than a week re-making.

values.title: Write it down
values.text: Line-item BOQs, signed variation notes and Friday photo reports. If it is not documented, it did not happen.

values.title: Make it ourselves
values.text: Joinery, metalwork and finishing happen in our own workshop, where we control the queue and the tolerance.

values.title: Stand behind it
values.text: Ten years on structure, twenty-four months on finishes and services, with scheduled returns at month three and month twelve.

values.title: One accountable name
values.text: A single project manager owns your programme, your budget and your phone calls from day one to handover.

values.title: Light before furniture
values.text: We design the lighting layers early. It is the cheapest thing to get right and the most expensive thing to fix later.

process.heroLead: No handover between a designer who disappears and a contractor who improvises. Each stage has defined outputs you sign off before the next one starts.
process.processText: Typical durations shown for a mid-size commercial project. A single-room renovation compresses to four weeks; a large home expands to thirty.
process.splitText: One report, one thread, one person accountable. It is the least glamorous part of what we do and the reason our on-programme rate is 97%.
process.splitText2: You will always know what happened this week, what happens next week, what decision we need from you, and any risk we can see coming.
